video.title: Denver Nuggets Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]

summary: Josh Lloyd previews the Denver Nuggets for fantasy in the 2026-27 season. His main question is whether the new pieces fit together now that Peyton Watson is gone and DeMar DeRozan has arrived. Nikola Jokic is still his number one fantasy player, and he would take Jokic first overall. He calls Jamal Murray a comfortable mid-second-round pick after a career year. He is avoiding Aaron Gordon in standard leagues because of injuries, and he stays skeptical of Christian Braun. His late swing pick is Cam Johnson. DeRozan is a value at his Yahoo rank but a fade inside the top 100 on ESPN, and Trayvon Brazil is a stash for dynasty and keeper leagues. Denver's schedule is good, with few back-to-backs.

rules.text: Small gaps between draft slot and final finish do not matter. Taking a player at 10 who finishes 15th is fine.
rules.quote: If you take someone at 10 and they finish 15th, it doesn't really matter.

rules.text: Skip low-upside veterans in the late rounds of standard drafts. Take flyers on young players or rookies with upside instead.
rules.quote: that perfect Tobias Harris pencil Harrison Barnes Bari type region of a draft which is like no-go zone

rules.text: Have a rationale for every pick: what the upside is, and how likely it is to improve on the alternatives.
rules.quote: every sort of pick and decision that you make, you got to have a rationale behind it

rules.text: He recommends using March 28th as the schedule end date when counting games, instead of Yahoo's default of April 4th.
rules.quote: If you're using my recommended schedule end date, which is March 28th, they have 443.

player_notes.text: He has pick one in a head-to-head categories league and will take Jokic there. Jokic is ranked 2nd on Yahoo and 1st on ESPN and goes pick one or two.
player_notes.quote: He's ranked number two on Yahoo this season. He's number one on ESPN.

player_notes.text: He has been the best fantasy player over the last five or six years and finished number one in category and points leagues.
player_notes.quote: The best fantasy player over the last five, six years, I guess. He was number one in category leagues.

player_notes.text: He had a hamstring injury two years ago and a somewhat fluky knee injury last season. There is a hope that at age 31 his injuries do not tick up.
player_notes.quote: Hopefully the hamstring injury from two years ago, we saw then we had a knee injury last season

player_notes.text: His threes, minutes and steal rate regressed last season as predicted. He is not very worried about more regression and expects about 35 minutes again.
player_notes.quote: 35 minutes a game last season, I think he does similar stuff.

player_notes.text: He had the best season of his career, with career highs in scoring and assists and usage up from 24 to 28. He finished 17th.
player_notes.quote: Murray was 17th last season. He averaged 25 4 and seven. Like those assist numbers are the best numbers

player_notes.text: He is a strong three-point shooter, close to 40% or better over the last four years. Shooting around 40 to 41% is a reasonable expectation going forward.
player_notes.quote: he's been close to 40% well the last four years 40 43 39 44 so 41 or 40 is reasonable

player_notes.text: His ESPN rank of 31 is free real estate. He is ranked 17 on Yahoo with an ADP of 21. He is comfortable taking Murray in the middle of the second round and fine with taking him as early as the start of round two.
player_notes.quote: I don't understand why his ESPN is 31 that is absolute free real estate on Yahoo he's at 17
player_notes.value_hint: Yahoo rank 17, ADP 21, ESPN 31; mid-second round

player_notes.text: His usage spiked under David Adelman. Many teammate absences also helped him, since Murray was the only one who stayed healthy.
player_notes.quote: Murray the only guy that really stayed healthy. So that that did benefit him.

player_notes.text: His body is breaking down with soft tissue injuries, including repeated hamstring and calf injuries.
player_notes.quote: his body, unfortunately for him, is starting to betray him soft tissue wise.

player_notes.text: He is not touching Gordon in standard formats. Gordon finished 146th in categories and is drafted around 112 to 119 on Yahoo. He sees no upside at that price.
player_notes.quote: drafted, 119 on Yahoo ranking, 112 ADP, I'm not touching that.

player_notes.text: He expects Denver to be extra cautious with Gordon's minutes. Gordon will be streamable but carries injury risk.
player_notes.quote: they're going to have to be extra cautious about Gordon and the way that they use him.

player_notes.text: He has poor shooting volume and creates spacing issues. His defense is overrated, he is not a stat generator, and he has been a low-usage player his whole career.
player_notes.quote: He creates so many spacing issues for this team with his inability to shoot. His defense is overrated.

player_notes.text: He is expected to start. His Yahoo ADP is 120 and his rank is 143. He should beat last season's finish outside the top 200, but the speaker is still not buying.
player_notes.quote: You can ignore his Yahoo ADP at 120. He's ranked at 143 and he was outside the top 200

player_notes.text: If anyone gives up minutes to DeRozan, it will most likely be Braun.

player_notes.text: He is an elite shooter who does little else: threes, free throws at a good percentage, and solid field goal percentage. He is now 30 with ankle and hip injury history.
player_notes.quote: Cam Johnson, who is now 30 with injuries everywhere, ankles, hips, all that sort of stuff

player_notes.text: He is a great scorer, but teams must make accommodations for him on offense and defense. He has spacing and defensive limitations.
player_notes.quote: having Demard Rozen on your team means that you need to make accommodations for Demar on offense and on defense.

player_notes.text: He projects to play the most bench minutes, likely in a lower-minute role. There is worry about the minutes he shares with Jokic.
